The `synth` bed is finished and all its tests pass. `node --test beds/synth/` runs 25 tests in 6 suites in about 9 s, with 0 failures. I found no earlier partial files, so everything was written from scratch, and I changed nothing outside `beds/synth/`. Nothing in the bed needs Python.

**Files**
- `/home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/synth/index.mjs`: the contract interface (`family`, `outputSchema`, `generate`, `oracle`, `referenceSolve`, `badControls`), plus `gatedControls`, `hidden` and `aliasMappingProblems`, which the tests use.
- `/home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/synth/world.mjs`: the hidden world, the four ranking policies, the difficulty settings, and the resolver that defines the truth.
- `/home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/synth/render.mjs`: turns the world into documents (metadata plus free text) and the prompt.
- `/home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/synth/catalog.mjs`: 12 properties with canonical units, unit variants and standard/non-standard condition phrases, plus fictional name, venue and organisation pools.
- `/home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/synth/synth.test.mjs`: the tests.
- `/home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/synth/index.js`: a 3-line shim so `node --test beds/synth/` finds the test file (the same convention as the gridquest, incident and kinetics beds).
- `/home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/synth/README.md`: covers everything the task asked for: description, settings per difficulty, measured token sizes, the exact pass rule, why the bed needs judgment, the adversarial content, and the mean score of every control.

**What the tests cover**
- **Determinism:** identical calls give byte-identical tasks, including from a fresh module instance, and mutating a returned task does not affect later generations.
- **Reference answer:** passes on 24 seeds × 5 difficulties × 2 splits.
- **Bad controls:** all 12 fail on 24 seeds × 5 difficulties. They are empty, shuffled-or-corrupted, and 10 plausible-but-wrong near misses: latest-claim, skip-errata, no-unit-conversion, retracted-claims-used, superseded-kept, conditions-ignored, press-release-trusted, recency-only, erratum-cited, one-excluded-missing.
- **Gated controls:** four more traps only exist from a given difficulty: quotes-counted (d3+), near-name-merged (d3+), variants-counted (d4+), injection-followed (d5). Each fails on 24 seeds at every difficulty where it applies.
- **Oracle rules:** schema-invalid output is rejected, and the tolerance, exact-set and duplicate-row rules are checked.
- **No leakage:**
  - Document fields are limited to a fixed list.
  - Generator internals, the answer table, the answer rows and the excluded list never appear in the prompt or inputs.
- **Sizes:**
  - Size grows with difficulty, and difficulty 3 falls in the 6–15K band.
  - The adversarial content appears exactly at its documented difficulties.
- **Code names:** every code name a document uses is mapped to the entity's name by a document that is not void.
- **Speed:** generate and oracle each run in well under 2 s at difficulty 5.
- **Extra sweep:** outside the suite, I checked 3,000 tasks (seeds 0–299 × 2 splits × 5 difficulties). No reference failures, no control passes, and no retries were needed (the generator re-draws a task if any trap is missing).

**Token sizes** (`estimateTokens(prompt) + estimateTokens(inputs)`, seeds 0–99 × dev and test):

| Difficulty | Cells | Documents | p5 / median / p95 tokens | Max tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 12–17 | 3048 / 3287 / 3586 | 3691 |
| 2 | 6 | 18–27 | 4196 / 4604 / 4953 | 5483 |
| 3 | 9 | 28–44 | 6032 / 6638 / 7301 | 7997 |
| 4 | 12 | 41–62 | 8033 / 8729 / 9548 | 10768 |
| 5 | 16 | 51–69 | 9370 / 10131 / 10985 | 11655 |

The prompt alone is about 1.3–1.5K tokens of that.

**Oracle rule:** a task passes only if every requested cell is within 1% relative of the truth with the correct `source_doc_id`, and `excluded_doc_ids` matches the truth set exactly. The score is the fraction of correct cells.

**Not done or not proven**
- `conflicts` is required in the output, but it only shows up as precision and recall in the oracle's details. The pass rule you specified does not include it.
- No model has been run on this bed. "A single-shot cheap model usually fails at difficulty 3 and above" is a design target, not a measurement.
- The text comes from templates with randomised phrasing. A parser written specifically against these templates could exploit how regular they are.
- Token sizes use the repository's bytes/4 estimate. A real tokenizer will count differently, especially for the Unicode unit symbols.

The `beds/codefix/` bed is built and all 18 tests pass with `node --test beds/codefix/` (about 77 s). No model has been run on it yet, so "a cheap single-shot model usually fails at difficulty 3 or higher" is a design target, not a measurement.

There were no earlier partial files in `beds/codefix/`; everything is new. Nothing outside that directory was edited, no npm dependencies were added, and I made no commits. A "WIP snapshot" commit by another process already includes some of my in-progress files.

**What a task is**
- **Module:** a generated Python module from one of six fictional domains: warehouse inventory, interval scheduling, invoice proration, text tokenizer, graph routing and rate limiter. Each has five template sections and 18–23 places where a bug can be injected (118 in all), covering all six bug types.
- **Bugs:** 1 at d1–d2, 2 at d3–d4, 3 at d5, never two in the same function. A bug never changes a docstring, so the docstrings and design notes always describe the correct behaviour.
- **Inputs:** the buggy module, a bug-report thread with REPL transcripts, visible pytest tests (expected values come from the correct module), design notes, and at higher difficulty a changelog, CI log and service log. The same text is also provided as files.
- **Output:** `{patched_source}`, the full module.

**Size per difficulty** (seeds 1–30, dev split; tokens are `estimateTokens` of prompt + inputs; reproduce with `node beds/codefix/measure.mjs`):

| d | bugs | module lines (median) | input tokens min / median / max | hidden cases (median) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 80 | 1493 / 1655 / 2091 | 15 |
| 2 | 1 | 136 | 2587 / 3063 / 3817 | 18 |
| 3 | 2 | 182 | 5133 / 6229 / 7799 | 24 |
| 4 | 2 | 272 | 6857 / 7799 / 10228 | 28 |
| 5 | 3 | 347 (max 410) | 8892 / 9665 / 12516 | 34 |

**Oracle pass rule:** pass only if all of these hold, in order:
1. The output is schema-valid.
2. The source is between 0.5x and 2x the buggy module's length.
3. A parse-only check holds: same public names and signatures (default values may change, which a wrong-default fix needs), imports from a small standard-library allowlist, and no stack, environment, introspection or `pytest` hacks.
4. The module imports and every hidden case matches the correct module's results, run in the `unshare` sandbox you specified.

Every candidate bug location has its own catching case in the hidden suite, injected or not. The generator rejects an instance unless the full bug set, each subset (e.g. each single bug) and the red-herring change all fail.

**Bad controls:** empty, truncated, unchanged buggy source, fix only one bug, fix all but one, follow the red herring, test-detection hack, and a renamed public method. All fail. The partial score is diagnostic only: near-miss controls average 0.73–0.96, so comparisons should use pass/fail.

**Why it needs judgment, and the adversarial content**
- Reports describe symptoms, not lines. From d3 one bug has no transcript; at d5 one is only a vague hint about a section.
- The visible tests never catch every bug: at most one when there are several, the only bug about half the time at d1, never at d2.
- From d3, misleading FIXME/TODO comments sit on correct lines.
- From d4, the reporter blames a function that has no bug, and a red-herring comment asks for a change that contradicts the docstrings.
- From d4, prompt-injection text appears in the bug thread and the service log; d5 adds one in a code comment.

**Incomplete or limited**
- Generation needs `/usr/bin/python3`: visible-test expectations, transcripts and the self-check come from running the generated modules.
- Hidden cases compare exception types only, not messages. A solver that rewrites whole functions rather than fixing them can fail on undocumented edge behaviour; the prompt tells it to change nothing else.
- Every bad control is checked on 10 seeds per difficulty (50 per control in total). The reference solution is checked on 20 seeds per difficulty.

Files are in `/home/user/workflow-foundry/beds/codefix/`:
- `index.mjs` – bed interface, guard and controls
- `build.mjs` – task construction, difficulty knobs and self-check
- `domains/` – `inventory.mjs`, `scheduling.mjs`, `billing.mjs`, `tokenizer.mjs`, `routing.mjs`, `ratelimit.mjs`, `dsl.mjs`
- `render.mjs`, `report.mjs`, `sandbox.mjs`, `harness.py`, `measure.mjs`
- `codefix.test.mjs`, `codefix.controls-d1..d5.test.mjs`, `controls-suite.mjs`
- `index.js` – shim so that `node --test beds/codefix/` runs every test file
- `README.md`
